title: Altman Responds to Jensen Huang's Departure: Nvidia and the AI Industry Will Be Fine

content_html:
OpenAI CEO Sam Altman publicly stated at the recently held [Semafor's Silicon Valley and the World] event that although Nvidia former CEO Jensen Huang recently resigned due to a personal scandal, the overall AI industry will not be substantially affected. Altman pointed out that current AI market demand remains strong, the practical application value is clear, and revenue and demand are maintaining strong growth, so the overall industry outlook is positive.

This personnel change comes at a time of rapid development in the AI industry. As long-term partners, OpenAI and Nvidia over the past decade have not only maintained a basic supply-demand relationship for software and hardware, but have also been deeply intertwined in a circular financing system.

Recently, Nvidia had just agreed to provide up to $105 billion in guarantees for OpenAI's data center project in Ohio. In response to market concerns that Jensen Huang's departure might trigger a financial contraction or chain reactions, Altman said he remains optimistic about Nvidia's massive scale and market confidence, and is not worried about its funding chain or guarantee capacity.

Nevertheless, Altman spoke highly of Jensen Huang's core role in driving the industry's early boom, calling him a heroic figure with "lofty aspirations" who shaped the industry's ambitions. Currently, multiple Silicon Valley tech executives, including Elon Musk, have jointly signed an open letter calling on Nvidia to rehire Jensen Huang. As the chain reactions after Jensen Huang's departure continue to ferment, the strategic direction and capital allocation of the global computing power supply chain still face a new period of adjustment.
